correctness.rationale: Mixed-basis Leibniz identities force twin-block symmetry, and characteristic-two square identities give blockwise zero row sum. A self-adjoint idempotent uniquely projects onto a nondegenerate subspace of the alternating sum-zero hyperplane. In even class sizes its one-dimensional radical contributes exactly q^(2r) lifts; in odd sizes the hyperplane is symplectic. Symplectic orbit-stabilizer gives q^(2r(h-r)) Gaussian_(q²)(h,r), multiplied over classes. Full defining-equation enumerations and finite-field block computations independently agree, but finite checks do not prove the universal theorem.

value.rationale: Projection derivations constitute a natural nonlinear operator invariant of the known evolution-algebra derivation spaces. The theorem delivers for all connected simple graphs an exact characteristic-two classification, a sharp even-rank spectrum, arithmetic multiplicities by symplectic Grassmannians and an edge-independent universality principle controlled solely by twin sizes. Nonisomorphic graphs share the same complete rank data, and the parity of twin sizes creates an explicit radical-line lift factor. This is an infinite-family exact result, not a small arbitrary numerical gain.
